description: Figure 1 is a four-panel composite that mixes two optical micrographs with two matching schematic illustrations. (a) is a colour optical micrograph of fully austenite low-density steel with a 50 µm scale bar, showing equiaxed polygonal grains annotated "Austentic grains" and straight, parallel-sided bands inside them annotated "Annealing twins"; faint white speckles are scattered over the field. (b) is a grayscale optical micrograph of austenite-based duplex low-density steel with a 20 µm scale bar and orthogonal RD/ND direction arrows at top right: a light grey "austenite matrix" labelled γ contains dark, elongated worm- or lentil-shaped inclusions annotated "Elongated ferrite grains", roughly aligned with RD. (c) and (d) are line schematics redrawing the same structures: (c) shows polygonal austenite grains with annealing twins labelled "Annealing twins" and "Austentic grains"; (d) shows a large austenitic grain field labelled "Austenitic grains" with wavy elongated white bands labelled "Ferrite grains". Together the panels argue that the annealed single-phase austenitic steel contains abundant annealing twins within fully recovered grains, whereas the duplex steel retains elongated ferrite grains aligned along the rolling direction. No numeric data are plotted; the only quantitative anchors are the 50 µm and 20 µm scale bars.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a colour optical micrograph of the fully austenite low-density steel carrying a 50 µm scale bar and two labels: "Austentic grains" and "Annealing twins".
In (a) the annealing twins appear as straight, parallel-sided bands cutting across equiaxed polygonal grains, a morphology distinct from the surrounding grain interiors.
Panel (b) is a grayscale optical micrograph with a 20 µm scale bar and orthogonal rolling-direction (RD) and normal-direction (ND) arrows in its top-right corner.
In (b) the light matrix is labelled "austenite matrix" with the symbol γ, and the dark thin elongated features inside it are labelled "Elongated ferrite grains".
The elongated ferrite grains in (b) are elongated roughly parallel to the RD arrow, i.e. along the rolling direction.

Panels (c) and (d) are line schematics that redraw the structures of the micrographs: (c) polygonal austenite grains containing straight twin bands, (d) austenitic grains containing elongated wavy ferrite bands.
The sample label in (a) is printed with a typographical error as "Austentic grains", whereas panel (d) prints "Austenitic grains" for the corresponding austenite phase.
No numeric data, axis values or property values are plotted anywhere in the figure; the only quantitative anchors are the 50 µm scale bar in (a) and the 20 µm scale bar in (b).

The caption states that (a) and (b) are optical microscope observations of a) fully austenite and b) austenite-based duplex low-density steels, and that (c) and (d) are illustrations of the same two steels.
The caption states the figure is adapted with permission from references [38,39], Copyright 2014 and 2015, Elsevier and Springer Nature.
The citing text asserts that abundant annealing twins are observed in the austenite low-density steel and that the grains are fully recovered.
The citing text asserts that elongated ferrite phase grains along the rolling direction are shown in the austenite-based duplex steel.
The bright white speckles scattered across panel (a) carry no label and are not explained by the caption.

subfigures.description: Colour optical micrograph of fully austenite low-density steel; 50 µm scale bar. Equiaxed polygonal grains annotated "Austentic grains" contain straight, parallel-sided bands annotated "Annealing twins"; small bright white speckles are scattered across the field. Grains appear in varied blue/violet to orange contrast.

Grayscale optical micrograph of austenite-based duplex low-density steel; 20 µm scale bar, with RD and ND arrows at top right. A light "austenite matrix" (labelled γ) contains dark, thin, elongated worm-like features annotated "Elongated ferrite grains" that are roughly aligned along RD.

Line schematic of the fully austenite structure: polygonal grain outlines with grain-boundary triple junctions, containing one or two straight parallel-sided grey bands per grain; annotated "Annealing twins" and "Austentic grains".
Line schematic of the duplex structure: a large light grey austenitic grain field annotated "Austenitic grains", traversed by elongated wavy white bands annotated "Ferrite grains".
